messages:
Anya (ML): FYI the eval harness blew up on the new runner patch when the query is empty. Repro on my laptop and CI.
Rami: ugh, do you have the stack/logs? which job failed?
Anya (ML): eng-ml/eval-runner job 72. small log snippet:```
2026-02-14T09:12:03Z ERROR runner::query - Empty query received
thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked at 'index out of bounds', src/runner/repr.rs:214
stack backtrace: ...
```
Anya (ML): it looks like we assume q[0] exists before tokenization fallback path
Rami: ok this explains the panic. empty query should be handled earlier. is this coming from dataset that has blank lines?
Anya (ML): yep a handful of MTEB-like datasets (noise in scraped examples) produce empty strings. Locally I fixed by filtering, but CI still runs unfiltered artifacts from preproc.
Kai: we should not filter silently at runner level — silent dropping changes metrics (MRR/NDCG) distribution. What do others think: treat empty query as skip + log, or return deterministic zero-embedding and let downstream reranker handle it?
Marta: returning zero-embedding will bias top-k retrieval (all zeros may tie). Skip with explicit counter + warn in metrics would be safest for consistency across evals. We need to record how many queries were dropped so dashboards show effective sample size.
eval-runner-bot: job eng-ml/eval-runner #72 failed: panic in runner::repr.rs:214. See https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/eng-ml/72 for logs.
Rami: agree with Marta. Add a pre-check in harness: if query.trim().is_empty() { increment counter; continue; } and emit a per-dataset dropped_queries metric. Also add an assert in unit tests to ensure we never panic on empty input.
Anya (ML): I'll open a tiny PR. Patch plan in comments:```diff
@@ -198,6 +198,12 @@ fn run_query(q: &str) -> Embedding {
-    let toks = tokenize(q)?;
-    let emb = encode(toks);
+    if q.trim().is_empty() {
+        METRICS.dropped_queries.inc();
+        warn!("empty query in dataset {}", dataset.name());
+        continue; // skip this query in eval loop
+    }
+    let toks = tokenize(q)?;
+    let emb = encode(toks);
 }
```
Kai: add a unit test covering: empty query in dataset, dataset-level sample count unaffected, dropped_queries increments, and overall MRR computation ignores dropped items (assert sample_size < total_lines when drops > 0). Also add e2e CI sample with one empty query in the synthetic dataset.
Marta: also update the dashboards: include `dropped_queries` on per-run panel and add an alert if dropped fraction > 1%. This will catch bad preprocessing going forward.
Anya (ML): PR opened: https://git.redwood-inference/p/eng-ml/runner/merge/1345 - includes code + tests + changelog entry. cc @Rami @Kai for review.
Rami: will review this morning. Quick thought: for downstream reporting we should annotate NDCG/MRR results with `effective_n` so that comparisons are apples-to-apples. Might tweak the eval report schema to include `{total_lines, dropped, effective_n}`.
Kai: agreed. That schema change must be backward compatible. Add new top-level fields to the JSON report and update the dashboard parsing.
Marta: can we add a CI check that prevents a regression: if dropped fraction increases by > 0.5% relative to baseline for this dataset, fail the job? Might be noisy but good to detect accidental preprocessing changes.
Anya (ML): for now I'll implement the filtering + metric + report fields. Follow-up issue for the CI gating work.
Rami: thanks. after merge we should re-run the failing job against the patched runner to validate the fix and generate a clean baseline for dashboards.
Anya (ML): re-run queued, will post results. :thumbsup:
